cards.explanation: The answer is that they flee and many fall. The men of Israel flee before the Philistines, and many fall slain on Mount Gilboa. It's a hard way to open the chapter, friends. The rest of this passage follows from this one battle.

The answer is False. Jonathan did not make it out. The Philistines hotly pursued Saul, Israel's king, and his sons, and they killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua. It's a sad verse, friends, so let it sit for a moment.

The answer is that Saul asks his armor-bearer to run him through with his sword. Saul tells him, “Draw your sword and run me through with it…” He says it because he fears the Philistines will come and torture him. It's a heavy moment, friends, and I think we should just let it be heavy.

The answer is True. The text says his armor-bearer “…was terrified and refused to do it.” Saul had asked him to draw his sword, and he wouldn't. After that, Saul takes his own sword. The text gives no reasons beyond the terror.

The answer is that they abandon their cities and run. The Israelites along the valley and across the Jordan saw that the army had fled and that Saul and his sons had died. So they abandoned their cities and ran away. That's what the text says, friends, plain and simple.

The answer is Philistines. When the Israelites abandoned their cities, the Philistines came and occupied them. These are the same people who fought Israel on Mount Gilboa. The text says it plainly, friends: the Philistines came and occupied their cities.

The answer is armor. The next day, the Philistines came to strip the dead, and they cut off Saul's head and stripped off his armor. This is a hard verse to read, friends. I think we can just say it's heavy and keep going.

The answer is in the temples of their idols. The Philistines sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to proclaim the news in the temples of their idols and among their people. That's where the messengers announce it, friends. The text names both places.
The answer is Beth-shan. The Philistines hung Saul's body on the wall of Beth-shan. His armor went into the temple of the Ashtoreths. It's a heavy detail, friends, and the text says it plainly.

The answer is that they bring the bodies back to Jabesh. All their men of valor set out, journeyed all night, and retrieved the bodies of Saul and his sons from the wall of Beth-shan. When they arrived at Jabesh, they burned the bodies there. The text doesn't say why they went, friends. I think this one is heavy, so let it be.

The answer is that they bury the bones under a tree in Jabesh. The men of Jabesh took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh. It's a quiet ending for a hard day, friends. They stayed with Saul and his sons even after everything.

The answer is True. After they buried the bones under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh, the men fasted seven days. The text gives us the number and nothing more, friends. I think it was a hard week for them.
